# RF-60 repair: one URL string per generated file, under the step 3 ruling at 144e053a3. The implementer's proof.
# Run on 2026-11-19 in the dev container (slot b, 12 processors), on repo/traits-flaky-1 at 144e053a3 with the repair
# in the working tree. Vite 8.4.0-beta.1, Vitest 5.1.0, Node v26.13.1. Scratch files weren't committed, and are deleted.
#
# ## The repair
#
# flattenToDir writes one more generated module, augmented.ts, with `export * from './<name>';` for each augmented
# trait module (`export {};` when there are none). Flattening.augmentedUrl is its file URL. No other module imports
# augmented.ts, and its relative specifiers are sent as the same root-relative URL strings as the consumers' imports.
# - flatten.node.test.ts, the brand row's block: the concurrent import(gen.url('checkable.ts')) and
#   import(gen.url('nameable.ts')) become one import(gen.augmentedUrl), still in the Promise.all with the consumers.
# - flatten-method.node.test.ts, the first block: import(gen.url('forwarding.ts')) becomes import(gen.augmentedUrl).
# - flattenToDir's documentation states the rule and its reason, and Flattening.url's says it is for the consumers only.
# Step 1's brandReport message is unchanged. No other test changes.
#
# ## 1. By reading: no file-URL import of a module that another module imports
#
# Every dynamic import( in packages/*/tests and .scripts whose specifier is built from gen., pathToFileURL, .href,
# new URL or augmentedUrl, fixtures excluded:
#   packages/material-x/tests/core/utils/polyfills.browser.test.ts:19:    await import(/* @vite-ignore */ url.href);
#   packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/flatten-composite.node.test.ts:33:      import(gen.url('foo-composed.ts')),
#   packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/flatten-composite.node.test.ts:34:      import(gen.url('foo-flat.ts')),
#   packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/flatten.node.test.ts:26:      import(gen.url('foo-composed.ts')),
#   packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/flatten.node.test.ts:27:      import(gen.url('foo-flat.ts')),
#   packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/flatten.node.test.ts:28:      import(gen.augmentedUrl),
#   packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/flatten.node.test.ts:117:      import(gen.url('foo-composed.ts')),
#   packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/flatten.node.test.ts:118:      import(gen.url('foo-flat.ts')),
#   packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/flatten-method.node.test.ts:20:    import(gen.url(`foo-composed${extension}`)),
#   packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/flatten-method.node.test.ts:21:    import(gen.url(`foo-flat${extension}`)),
#   packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/flatten-method.node.test.ts:43:    ({ Forwarding } = (await import(gen.augmentedUrl)) as {
#   .scripts/package-files.ts:59:  const { default: files } = await import(filesUrl.href, {
# - gen.url(...) names only foo-composed and foo-flat (with the consumer's extension). No generated module imports a
#   consumer, so each is requested under its file URL only.
# - gen.augmentedUrl names augmented.ts, which no module imports.
# - polyfills.browser.test.ts imports src/core/utils/polyfills.ts with the query ?fresh-import on purpose, to get a
#   fresh instance in the browser project. It is a different module by design, not a generated file, and the ruling's
#   property 4 leaves it.
# - .scripts/package-files.ts imports files.json natively in Node, outside Vitest's module runner.
#
# ## 2. The reproduction, rerun with the repair: 1,000 repeats in one worker, coverage, 24 busy-loop processes
#
#   RF60_REPEATS=1000 RF60_URL_LOG=<log> CI=true aube exec -- vitest run --project node/vite-traits-plugin \
#     --coverage.enabled --reporter=default --reporter=<url-reporter.ts> packages/vite-traits-plugin/tests/rf60-repro.node.test.ts
# The scratch test and the reporter are rf60-reproduction.txt's. The test's four imports become the repaired three:
#       const [composedMod, flatMod, traitsMod] = (await Promise.all([
#         import(gen.url('foo-composed.ts')),
#         import(gen.url('foo-flat.ts')),
#         import(gen.augmentedUrl),
#       ])) as [ … ];
#       const { Checkable, Nameable } = traitsMod;
#
#                                        before (rf60-reproduction.txt)   repaired           mutation (section 3)
#   repeats failed                       8 of 1,000                       0 of 1,000         10 of 1,000
#   files under two URL strings          478                              0                  525
#     of them checkable.ts               277                              0                  303
#     of them nameable.ts                201                              0                  222
#   requests for checkable.ts            1277                             1000               1303
#   requests for nameable.ts             1201                             1000               1222
#   requests for augmented.ts            0                                1000               0
# Repaired: each trait module is requested once per directory, as /tests/fixtures/gen-X/<name>, and no file in any
# directory is requested under two URL strings. The run took 78 s and passed.
# Mutation: all 10 failures are candidate (B) by step 1's message: 9 lost Checkable's brand and 1 Nameable's, and no
# chain carries an "undefined" key.
#
# ## 3. Mutation: the file-URL trait imports restored
#
# a. The reproduction with the step 2 test text unchanged, which imports checkable.ts and nameable.ts by file URL
#    concurrently with the consumers, under the same load and coverage, with the repaired helper: the third column
#    above. The two URL strings come back for 525 files, and 10 of 1,000 repeats fail.
# b. The committed flatten.node.test.ts with the brand row block's file-URL trait imports restored, run alone 20 times
#    with coverage and no load, and the repaired file run the same way 20 times. Neither showed a file under two URL
#    strings in 40 generated directories, and neither failed. A single run rarely overlaps the two requests, so this
#    doesn't discriminate. That is why (a) uses the reproduction's 1,000 repeats under load. Reverted: the file
#    matches the committed repair.
#
